summary: Joy Cecile Brennan works in Buddhist studies and philosophy. She earned her PhD at the University of Chicago, studying under Paul Mendes-Flohr, Richard Rosengarten, Constance Furey, and Diane Martin.

Juan Wu is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who completed a PhD at Cardiff University under doctoral supervisor Max Deeg (attested 2012). Wu held a postdoctoral post at the University of Tokyo (attested 2014).

Judit Törzsök specializes in Indology and religious studies. She studied at Eötvös Loránd University and the University of Oxford (DPhil) under Alexis Sanderson. She held posts at the University of Lille (2001) and École Pratique des Hautes Études (professor, 2018).

Judith Simmer-Brown specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied at Cornell College, Florida State University, Columbia University, and Walden University (PhD), and with traditional teacher Chögyam Trungpa. From 1977, she served as a professor at Naropa University.

Juhn Y. Ahn is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a PhD from the University of California, Berkeley in 2007. He held positions at the University of Michigan, serving as Associate Professor of Buddhist and Korean Studies by 2019.

Juhyung Rhi specializes in Buddhist studies and history and archaeology. He earned his PhD at the University of California, Berkeley, and became Professor of Art History at Seoul National University in 1992.
Juichiro Tanabe is a scholar in philosophy and other fields. He was a PhD candidate at the University of Bradford (2000–2001) and studied under traditional teacher Richard Hunn.

Jules Barthélemy-Saint-Hilaire (1805–1895) was a French scholar of philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Bourbon College and Collège Louis-le-Grand, and served as Professor of Greek at the Collège de France from 1838 to 1852.

Jules Bloch (1880–1953) specialized in Indology and linguistics. He studied under Sylvain Lévi and Antoine Meillet at EPHE and the University of Paris. His posts included EPHE (1919–1951), INALCO (1921–1937), and the Collège de France (1936–1951).

Jules Brooks Levinson specializes in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed a PhD at the University of Virginia in 1994 under Jeffrey Hopkins and was an assistant professor in the Department of Religion at Hamline University (attested 1996).

Jules Michelet (1798–1874) was a French historian who studied at Lycée Charlemagne. He held positions at the École Normale Supérieure, the Archives nationales (1831–1851), and the Collège de France as professor of history (1838–1852).

Jules Oppert (1825–1905) worked in history, archaeology, and linguistics. After earning a PhD from Kiel University in 1847, he was a professor of Sanskrit and comparative philology at INALCO (1857) and professor at the Collège de France (1874–1905).

Julia A. B. Hegewald (born 1971) works in Indology and history/archaeology. She completed BA and PhD degrees at SOAS University of London, an MA at Oxford, and a habilitation at RWTH Aachen, becoming professor at the University of Bonn in 2010.

Julia Ching (1934–2001) worked in sinology, religious studies, and philosophy. She studied at the College of New Rochelle, Catholic University of America, and Australian National University (PhD), and was appointed professor at the University of Toronto in 1978.

Julia F. Andrews (born 1951) is a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology. She studied at Brown University, Harvard University, and the University of California, Berkeley, and held a post at Ohio State University around 1987.
Julia Leslie (1948–2004) was a scholar in Indology and religious studies who held an academic post at SOAS University of London from around 1990 to 2004.

Juliane Schober works in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She completed her PhD at the University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign in 1989 and served as an associate professor of religious studies at Arizona State University (attested 2007).

Julie Gifford is a scholar of Buddhist studies and religious studies. She earned her PhD from the University of Chicago under doctoral supervisor Frank E. Reynolds and held a post at Miami University.
Julius Dutoit (1872–1958) was a scholar in the fields of Indology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teachers Adalbert Kuhn and Ernst Kuhn.

Julius Eggeling (1842–1918) was an Indologist who studied at Breslau and Berlin under Adolf Friedrich Stenzler and Albrecht Weber. He served as Secretary of the Royal Asiatic Society and was Professor at the University of Edinburgh (1875–1914).
